source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 25 January 1972, p. 3 ("SUPPORT FLOWING IN - FITT (Millar returned unopposed for Dock ward)"); Belfast News-Letter, 25 January 1972, p. 2 ("Council (Millar returned unopposed as councillor for Dock)"); Belfast Telegraph, 26 January 1972, p. 2 ("Aldermen not chosen at elections"); Belfast News-Letter, 22 February 1972, p. 5 ("Three to fight for Dock Ward (Millar described as unofficial Unionist councillor)")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph / Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Unopposed return at nomination (Monday 24 Jan 1972, 'yesterday' in the 25 Jan papers); no poll.

note: By-election of 24 January 1972 for one seat in Dock (Belfast County Borough Council), caused by the disqualification of Councillor Patrick (Paddy) Kennedy for non-attendance (News-Letter calls him SDLP; Civgraph's 1967 Dock file has P. Kennedy, Republican Labour). Returned unopposed: no poll was held.

countGroup.Party_Basis: Put up by the Dock Unionist Association; the Belfast News-Letter of 22 February 1972 (p. 5) calls him an unofficial Unionist councillor
